Events (DOM Standard: EventTarget, Event; UI Events: MouseEvent, KeyboardEvent). Any node and any host object (a promise, a socket, a worker, an abort signal...) is an EventTarget. An Event handle is valid while its listeners run.

Exposed to: Window, Worker. Source: api/events.widl.

Odin: import "wren:core".

#Types

#handle EventTarget

A node or a host object: whatever can have listeners. Checked by the functions that take it.

#handle Event

The event being dispatched.

Checked by the browser on every call (lookup_Event).

#flags ListenerOptions : u32

addEventListener options.

memberbit
Capture0Run in the capture phase.
Once1Remove the listener after its first call.
Passive2The listener will not call preventDefault.

#flags EventInit : u32

What dispatchEvent creates.

memberbit
Bubbles0
Cancelable1
Composed2The event crosses shadow roots: its path goes on to the hosts (targets retargeted).
Activation3A MouseEvent: a click runs the activation behaviour of what it targets (DOM dispatch's activation target: a check box toggles, a label clicks its control, a link is followed).

#callback EventListener

void EventListener(i32 user, Event event)

A listener: user is the value given to addEventListener.

delta_yf64
delta_zf64

buttonsu32MouseEvent.buttons

repeatu32KeyboardEvent.repeat
delta_modeu32WheelEvent.deltaMode
pointer_idi32PointerEvent.pointerId (1 for the mouse)
pointer_typeu32PointerEvent.pointerType: 0 mouse, 1 pen, 2 touch
is_primaryu32PointerEvent.isPrimary
pressuref64PointerEvent.pressure, tangentialPressure
tangential_pressuref64
widthf64PointerEvent.width / height (CSS px)
heightf64
tilt_xf64PointerEvent.tiltX / tiltY / twist (degrees)
tilt_yf64
twistf64

#EventTarget_addEventListener

i32 EventTarget_addEventListener(EventTarget target, string type, EventListener callback, i32 user = 0, ListenerOptions options = none) raises

target.addEventListener(type, listener, options). Returns the listener's id (for removeEventListener); adding the same (type, callback, user) again returns the existing id.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: EventTarget_addEventListener :: proc(c: ^Call, target: u64, type: string, callback: u32, user: i32, options: Api_ListenerOptions) -> (i32, Api_Error)

#PointerCapture_set

void PointerCapture_set(Element element, i32 pointer_id) raises

Element.setPointerCapture(pointerId): Not_Found for a pointer that is not active, Invalid_State for an element that is not connected. The capture takes effect at the pointer's next event (gotpointercapture).

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: PointerCapture_set :: proc(c: ^Call, element: Api_Element, pointer_id: i32) -> Api_Error

#EventTarget_dispatchEngineEvent

bool EventTarget_dispatchEngineEvent(EventTarget target, string type, EventInit init, i64 engine_id, f64 time_stamp) raises

target.dispatchEvent(event) for an Event the engine owns: like EventTarget_dispatchEvent, with the engine's identifier of the object (Event_engineId gives it back to the listeners) and its timeStamp. Returns false when a listener cancelled it. The event is not trusted (isTrusted is false).

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: EventTarget_dispatchEngineEvent :: proc(c: ^Call, target: u64, type: string, init: Api_EventInit, engine_id: i64, time_stamp: f64) -> (bool, Api_Error)
